title: Committee of Supply − Head U (Prime Minister's Office)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply − Head U (Prime Minister's Office)

sections.label: Public Service praised as world-class
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore's Public Service is the envy of the world and recalls a foreign government wanting to buy a Statutory Board.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Our Public Service is, indeed, the envy of the world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: It has done very well and I am even reminded of a story − there was a certain foreign government which wanted to buy an entire Statutory Board from Singapore.

sections.label: Central pooling of procurement needs
sections.summary: The Government can leverage scale to procure more smartly if Ministries pool major procurement needs centrally.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Here, the Government has the ability to leverage on scale to procure more smartly if every Ministry could pool their major procurement needs centrally.

sections.label: One secure mobile app for transactions
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Singaporeans could soon use one secure mobile app to transact with every Government department, linked to the private sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Would it be possible one day, and hopefully soon, for Singaporeans to hold just one secure mobile app to transact − transact meaning to apply, to be informed, to pay, to receive and so on − with every Government department which is also linked to the private sector.

sections.label: Managing strategic resources and trade-offs
sections.summary: As the economy matures, strategic resources like manpower, land, energy and water must be managed better because of trade-offs between Ministries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cedric Foo Chee Keng (Pioneer)
sentences.text: Increasingly, as our economy matures, our strategic resources like manpower, land, energy and water must be managed better for there are trade-offs when used by one Ministry versus another.

sections.label: MINDEF I-Net System data breach
sections.summary: MINDEF's I-Net System was breached, stealing personal data of over 850 National Servicemen and employees; the Deputy Secretary called it targeted and well-planned.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For example, earlier this week, it was reported that MINDEF's I-Net System was breached.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The personal data of more than 850 National Servicemen and employees were stolen, which included their NRIC numbers, telephone numbers and dates of birth.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: MINDEF's Deputy Secretary said that the attack and breach were targeted and well-planned, and that they could not have been the work of casual hackers or criminal gangs.

sections.label: Preparing public officers, hiring engineers
sections.summary: The passage asks PMO how the Public Service is prepared for capabilities like cybersecurity, and notes 1,000 more engineers and higher salaries were announced.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Given the current interest and emphasis on building new and strategic capabilities in areas, such as cybersecurity and intelligence, data analytics, and digital and software engineering, I would like to ask PMO how are our Public Service and public officers being prepared to stay ahead of the curve?

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: He announced that the Public Service will employ an additional 1,000 engineers and raise the salaries of our public sector engineers to attract and retain engineering officers in the Service.

sections.label: Employment of persons with disabilities
sections.summary: The speaker notes a year has passed since plans to employ persons with disabilities were announced, and describes a PSD website search for "inclusive".

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I also recognised that the final employment decisions are rightly left to the respective agencies but, nonetheless, observed that unless the human resource teams of PSD and the respective agencies share the same values and commitment as our political leaders and the Head of the Civil Service, we will see very little progress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It has been a year since the Government announced plans to employ persons with disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On Sunday, I did a search on the website of PSD on the word "inclusive" just to see if I could find any progress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It returned 14 results, including one search result for "inclusive of GST".

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The next was Minister Tan Chuan-Jin giving his speech at the Singapore HR Awards in 2016 for the employment of persons with disabilities by public agencies.

sections.label: Public Sector Transformation journey
sections.summary: In 2012 the Public Service began Public Sector Transformation to focus on the citizen and community under the vision "One Trusted Public Service with Citizens at the Centre".

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In 2012, the Public Service embarked on a journey of Public Sector Transformation to evolve their approaches with a laser focus on the citizen and community, to realise the vision of "One Trusted Public Service with Citizens at the Centre".

sections.label: Digital technologies and data capabilities
sections.summary: The speaker asks what the Government is doing to build strategic capabilities using digital technologies and data while addressing legislative, security and privacy concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The whole-of-Government needs to leverage on the power of digital technologies and data to fundamentally re-imagine and transform our capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: So, I wish to ask the Minister what is the Government doing to build such strategic capabilities while circumventing legislative, security and privacy concerns, and how can these translate into better outcomes for Singapore and Singaporeans?

sections.label: Committee on the Future Economy
sections.summary: The Committee on the Future Economy recommended that Singaporeans continue to acquire and utilise deep skills.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: The Committee on the Future Economy recommended that Singaporeans continue to acquire and utilise deep skills.

sections.label: Public Service officers' skills
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Government will ensure Public Service officers have the right skills to deliver public services effectively.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: How will the Government ensure that Public Service officers have the right skills to deliver public services effectively?

sections.label: Support for older officers
sections.summary: The passage asks how the diverse and inclusive sector will support all employees, especially older officers, and how innovation will be instilled as roles are outsourced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: How will the diverse and inclusive sector provide all its employees, especially the older officers, with the necessary support to perform to their fullest potential?

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: As portions of roles within the Civil Service get outsourced, we should end up with a trimmer and leaner workforce.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Still, how do we instil the spirit and standards of innovation in the Civil Service workforce nonetheless?

sections.label: Carbon tax revenue funding emissions measures
sections.summary: A carbon tax is an important move towards climate change resilience, and Minister Heng said revenue will help fund industry measures to reduce emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The introduction of a carbon tax is an important move towards climate change resilience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Minister Heng has stated that revenue from carbon tax will help to fund measures by industries to reduce emissions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Does this mean that the revenue will be ring-fenced and channelled back to these purposes?

sections.label: Revenue supporting sustainable consumption culture
sections.summary: The passage asks whether revenue could support these movements, amplify their voices, and create a culture of sustainable consumption and production beyond a carbon tax.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the revenue be used to support these movements, have their voices amplified, and to create a culture of sustainable consumption and production that goes far beyond a carbon tax?

sections.label: Singapore emissions intensity reduction pledge
sections.summary: Singapore is a Party to the Agreement and pledged to reduce emissions intensity by 36% from 2005 levels by 2030 and stabilise emissions, aiming to peak around 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Singapore is a Party to the Agreement and has pledged to reduce emissions intensity by 36% from 2005 levels by 2030, and stabilise our emissions with the aim of peaking around 2030.

sections.label: Carbon tax implementation from 2019
sections.summary: The Minister for Finance announced in the Budget Speech that the Government will aim to implement a carbon tax from 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The Minister for Finance has announced in the Budget Speech that the Government will aim to implement a carbon tax from 2019.

sections.label: Carbon tax revenue not earmarked
sections.summary: The carbon tax revenue will not be earmarked for specific purposes to retain flexibility.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The carbon tax revenue will not be earmarked for specific purposes to retain flexibility.

sections.label: Industry consultations on carbon tax
sections.summary: Industry consultations on the carbon tax have already begun and will be expanded.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Industry consultations on the carbon tax have already begun and will be expanded.

sections.label: Growing GovTech and CSA professionals
sections.summary: A core group of 250 professionals in GovTech and the Cyber Security Agency will be grown to drive key digital capabilities in the Public Service.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: We need to build up our IT professional workforce to support priority areas.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: We will grow a core group of 250 professionals in GovTech and Cyber Security Agency to drive key digital capabilities in areas, such as data science and cybersecurity, in the Public Service.

sections.label: Training public officers in digital capabilities
sections.summary: 10,000 public officers will be trained over the next four years in digital capabilities such as data analytics, data science and cybersecurity.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: We also need a broader appreciation and application of these new technologies in the Public Service as a whole.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: We will, therefore, be training 10,000 public officers over the next four years in digital capabilities, such as using more data analytics and data science in policy formulation, service delivery, corporate services and strengthening cybersecurity.

sections.label: Three Centres of Excellence announced
sections.summary: Last year, the establishment of three Centres of Excellence was announced: JTC, GovTech and DSTA.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Last year, I announced the establishment of three Centres of Excellence (CentExs) − JTC, GovTech and DSTA.

sections.label: New CentExs for caverns and tunnelling
sections.summary: This year, capabilities were built up in two new CentExs: JTC for underground caverns and LTA for tunnelling.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Some issues are further from the public eye, but no less important.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: This year, we built up capabilities in two new CentExs − JTC for underground caverns and LTA for tunnelling.

sections.label: Public Service engineer recruitment numbers
sections.summary: The Public Service recruited over 1,000 engineers last year, bringing the total to close to 9,000.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The Public Service recruited over 1,000 engineers last year, bringing the total to close to 9,000.

sections.label: Civil Service College digital training partnership
sections.summary: The Civil Service College will partner agencies and external providers such as Coursera to train 10,000 officers in digital capabilities.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: For example, as I had mentioned, the Civil Service College will partner agencies and external providers, such as Coursera, to train 10,000 officers in digital capabilities.

sections.label: Public sector re-employment wage reductions
sections.summary: From 1 July 2017, wage reductions on re-employment for public sector officers re-employed to the same job grade will be removed after review and union consultation.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: Following our latest review and in consultation with the public sector unions, from 1 July 2017, we will remove wage reductions on re-employment for public sector officers re-employed to the same job grade.

sections.label: Public Service disabled employment
sections.summary: The Public Service had employed about 270 persons with disabilities by end 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Coordinating Minister for National Security (Mr Teo Chee Hean)
sentences.text: The Public Service has employed about 270 persons with disabilities by end 2016.

sections.label: Budget supports Industry Transformation Roadmap
sections.summary: The Budget has supported the CFE's recommendation to help businesses transform through the Industry Transformation Roadmap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Budget has supported the CFE's recommendation to help businesses transform through the Industry Transformation Roadmap.

sections.label: Automation risk to jobs
sections.summary: A McKinsey report said 45% of paid activities can be automated, and in Singapore 27,000 taxis, 100,000 taxi licences and 12,000 bus driver roles are at risk.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: A November 2015 report by McKinsey explained that in a survey of 800 jobs and 2,000 activities, 45% of activities that individuals are presently paid to perform can be automated by adapting currently demonstrated technologies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In Singapore's context, if I take the threat of autonomous vehicles as an example, we have possibly 27,000 taxis, or 100,000 taxi vocational driver licences, and 12,000 bus driver roles at risk.

sections.label: Government platforms for innovation
sections.summary: The question asks what platforms and initiatives the Government will drive to enable Singaporeans and businesses to innovate, thrive and achieve better quality of life.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: What platforms and initiatives will the Government be driving to enable and encourage Singaporeans and businesses to innovate, thrive and achieve better quality of life?

sections.label: Spending and usage of apps
sections.summary: The question asks how much Ministries spent to develop and market these apps and their actual monthly usage.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: How much money have our Ministries spent to develop and market these apps and what is the actual monthly usage of them?

sections.label: National Identity system possibility
sections.summary: The Prime Minister mentioned the possibility of a National Identity system at the Camp Sequoia dialogue last month.

sentences.speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister also mentioned the possibility of a National Identity system at the Camp Sequoia dialogue last month.

sections.label: Dubai drone service and smart domains
sections.summary: Dubai is piloting the world's first passenger-carry drone service in July, and five domains were identified where technology could change things.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: Dubai, on the other hand, is piloting to launch the world's first passenger-carry drone service in July this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: How are we setting ourselves apart from other cities looking to be "smart"?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: We have identified five domains where technology could significantly change how things are done.

sections.label: Smart Nation enabled living questions
sections.summary: Questions were asked on Smart Nation plans for enabled living, pilot project updates, enabling elderly and disabled persons, and assistive technology training.

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: My questions are: what are our plans under the Smart Nation initiative to use technology in enabled living?

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: Could we have an update on the effect of the pilot projects?

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: How do we enable living, enable employment, enable community participation by persons who are elderly or persons who have disabilities and special needs?

sentences.speaker: Ms Chia Yong Yong
sentences.text: What plans do we have either for the Enabling Village or for other platforms to reach out to more schools and to train more professionals, and even ordinary persons, to be able to have some basic knowledge about assistive technology and, in some cases, even to provide advice on assistive technology?

sections.label: Disruption of white collar work
sections.summary: It will disrupt hitherto safe middle-class white collar work and impact wages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: But, let me start with a more serious note.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: It is going to disrupt even hitherto safe middle-class white collar work, and it will impact wages.

sections.label: Smart Nation priority is jobs
sections.summary: Similar changes are happening in surgery, legal and accounting professions, so Smart Nation's top priority has to be jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The same thing is happening in surgery and similar things are happening in the legal and accounting professions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And so, the top priority for Smart Nation has to be jobs, jobs, jobs.

sections.label: Digital identity project
sections.summary: One big project being worked on now is digital identity.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: One big project we are working on now is digital identity.

sections.label: Central Addressing Scheme for transfers
sections.summary: A Central Addressing Scheme being rolled out with industry maps mobile numbers to bank account numbers or business entity numbers to facilitate digital cash transfers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: For instance, if I want to transfer to you, I need to know your bank account number.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We are working with the industry to roll out a Central Addressing Scheme, which will better enable or facilitate digital cash transfers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: This works like a register which maps mobile numbers to bank account numbers, or to the unique entity number of businesses.

sections.label: Interoperability and Central Addressing Scheme
sections.summary: Interoperability is needed for convenience, lower barriers to entry and security, and a Central Addressing Scheme is one way to advance e-payments in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: But we need interoperability so that it becomes convenient, there are lower barriers to entry and it is secure.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We believe that having a Central Addressing Scheme is one way to get a move-on with e-payments in Singapore.

sections.label: Public transport data downloads
sections.summary: Public transport data is downloaded about 16 million times a day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: In fact, today, public transport data is downloaded about 16 million times a day.

sections.label: Pre-booking seats on selected routes
sections.summary: Seats can be pre-booked on 15 selected routes identified using data from a crowd-starting platform developed and provided by GovTech.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: You can pre-book seats on 15 selected routes and these are identified using data from a "crowd-starting" platform − developed and provided by GovTech.

sections.label: URA ePlanner geospatial portal
sections.summary: URA developed ePlanner, a digital portal aggregating geospatial data, supporting planners from 25 partner agencies to access and analyse land use planning information and decide based on data.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: URA developed ePlanner, a one-stop digital portal that aggregates large volumes of geospatial data and it supports planners from 25 different partner agencies who can now collectively access and analyse land use planning information and make decisions objectively on the basis of data, not on the basis of opinion.

sections.label: URA SPACE online map portal
sections.summary: In June last year, URA revamped URA SPACE, an online map portal consolidating detailed land use information, including private property-related information.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Another example is, in June last year, URA revamped the URA SPACE, which is an online map portal that consolidates detailed land use information, including private property-related information.

sections.label: Remote monitoring pilot homes
sections.summary: Remote monitoring solutions are being piloted in homes in Yuhua, Marine Parade and Bedok.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: For homes, we are piloting remote monitoring solutions in places like Yuhua, Marine Parade and Bedok.

sections.label: Tech Able outreach numbers
sections.summary: Tech Able has reached out to about 3,000 people thus far.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Tech Able has reached out to about 3,000 people thus far.

sections.label: Vision for technology and society
sections.summary: The passage states the aim is maximising future job options, better quality of life and an inclusive society, with a vision for visitors to Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Ultimately, this is not about technology but really about maximising future job options and ensuring a better quality of life and an inclusive society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Our vision is that a visitor to Singapore should come, look, experience and say, "I have seen the future and it works."

sections.label: Singapore TFR decline and rise
sections.summary: Singapore's TFR declined from the 1950s and 1960s to a historic low of 1.15 in 2010, later rising above 1.19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Likewise, for Singapore, TFR has declined steadily from the 1950s and 1960s, reaching a historic low of 1.15 in 2010.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Subsequent years have seen the rate rise above 1.19, with highs of 1.29 in 2012 and 1.25 in 2014.

sections.label: New citizens political party exposure
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Government will expose new citizens to other political parties and educate them on secret voting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Will the Government find ways to expose new citizens to members of other political parties and, more importantly, will it include an element of education to train them how their votes are kept secret in the electoral process?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: If it is in doubt, can we conduct a study to ascertain whether the new citizens truly understand that their votes are kept secret?

sections.label: Childcare centre demand and waiting lists
sections.summary: The passage notes demand-supply mismatch, year-long waiting lists, and asks how the Ministry gauges demand before building childcare centres.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Sometimes, this is because of the mismatch between demand and supply.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I have had parents coming to say that they have had to put their children on year-long waiting lists, sometimes even longer.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: How does the Ministry gauge the demand before it begins building these childcare centres?

sections.label: SkillsFuture Credit for residents' courses
sections.summary: Asks whether SkillsFuture Credit can be used to attend such courses for residents.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Can we tap on SkillsFuture Credit to attend such courses for the residents?

sections.label: Transforming employers' mindset, private sector
sections.summary: Asks what can be done to transform employers' mindset and get more private sector employers on board.

sentences.speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
sentences.text: What can be done to transform the employers' mindset and get more employers from the private sector on board?

sections.label: Punggol births in 2016
sections.summary: States that in 2016 an average of nine babies were born daily to Punggol residents, 10% of Singaporean babies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: On average, nine babies were born every day to residents of Punggol in 2016, accounting for 10% of Singaporean babies born last year.

sections.label: Infantcare options and MOE childcare
sections.summary: Asks whether new towns can have more infantcare options and whether MOE can undertake childcare provision.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: For instance, can there be more infantcare options in new towns, given the mismatch in demand and supply even as the Ministry has announced an increase in infantcare positions?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Further, can MOE also undertake childcare provision, since it is childcare that young parents most desperately need and want, and not kindergartens?

sections.label: Baby Boomers' children child-bearing years
sections.summary: States that large cohorts of the children of the Baby Boomers are entering their child-bearing years.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sun Xueling
sentences.text: Large cohorts of the children of the Baby Boomers are entering their child-bearing years.

sections.label: Resident's childcare placement plea
sections.summary: Recounts a resident's plea over finding childcare, citing a waiting list of at least 50 and costly or distant centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Just earlier today, I received yet another plea from a resident who fretted over finding a childcare placement for her child because the childcare centre at her void deck had put her on a waiting list of at least 50, and the other childcare centres were either too expensive or too far away.

sections.label: Early childhood programme economic returns
sections.summary: Heckman and researchers found high quality early childhood programmes can deliver a 13% annual return per child on upfront costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Nobel-winning economist James Heckman and researchers at the University of Chicago and University of Southern California found that high quality early childhood development programmes can deliver an annual return of 13% per child on upfront costs through better outcomes in education, health, employment and social behaviour in the decades that follow.

sections.label: PPHS flats for unsuccessful couples
sections.summary: A speaker suggests offering unutilised PPHS flats to first-timer married couples unsuccessful in balloting for a flat twice.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The introduction of the Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS)was a wonderful scheme that addresses this challenge.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But it is not fully utilised and I understand that there are still PPHS flats waiting to be taken.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Instead of leaving them empty, could we offer PPHS to first-timer married couples who were unsuccessful in balloting for a flat but had already participated in the ballots, say, twice?

sections.label: Shortage of smaller PPHS flats
sections.summary: A speaker says there are not enough smaller PPHS flats and larger ones are out of young couples' budgets.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: I believe that priority is already given to families in HDB's BTO scheme and there is the PPHS that Ms Tin Pei Ling mentioned earlier, for those who already have a flat but are waiting for their flat to arrive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: However, I understand that there is not enough smaller PPHS flats to meet the needs of these young couples and young families, and while they would be willing to consider the larger PPHS flats, they find that these flats are out of their budget.

sections.label: Scheduling software and Work-Life Grant
sections.summary: A speaker encourages the Government to enhance the Work-Life Grant and share technological solutions with companies, especially smaller SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Employee scheduling software takes away the tedium of rostering.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: I encourage the Government to enhance the Work-Life Grant and share technological solutions with companies, especially the smaller SMEs, to boost FWA adoption.

sections.label: Paid caregiving leave structure
sections.summary: A speaker states that the current paid caregiving leave structure is rather disjointed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Our current paid caregiving leave structure is rather disjointed.

sections.label: Childcare leave by child's age
sections.summary: Childcare leave is reduced from six days for ages 0-6, to four days for 7-9, and two days for 10-12.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Childcare leave is progressively reduced from six days when a child is 0-6 years old, four days from 7-9 years old, and to two days from 10-12 years old.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements uptake
sections.summary: The proportion of firms offering unplanned time-off or ad hoc teleworking rose from 70% in 2015 to 77% last year, and employees in firms with at least one formal FWA rose from 65% in 2016 to 67%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The results indicate that the proportion of firms which provided unplanned time-off or ad hoc teleworking for their employees rose from 70% in 2015 to 77% last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The proportion of employees working in firms offering at least one formal FWA rose from 65% in 2016 to 67% last year.

sections.label: Development Grant and FWA incentive
sections.summary: Under the Development Grant, employers receive $10,000 for piloting at least two new FWAs or substantially enhancing existing FWAs, and under the FWA incentive, $10,000 for the first five Singaporean employees utilising FWAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Currently, under the Development Grant, employers receive $10,000 for piloting at least two new FWAs or substantially enhancing existing FWAs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Under the FWA incentive, employers get $10,000 for the first five Singaporean employees utilising FWAs.

sections.label: Immigration and prime working ages
sections.summary: There are about 2.2 million citizens aged 20 to 64 today, and without immigration this segment will fall by close to 10%, or about 200,000, by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: At the same time, we welcome those who are committed to Singapore and are able to contribute to society as new residents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: There are about 2.2 million citizens today in the prime working ages of 20 to 64 years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Without immigration, the size of this segment of our population will fall by close to 10%, or about 200,000 by 2030.

sections.label: Old-age support ratio decline
sections.summary: The OASR will decline from five today to two in 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Our OASR will decline from five today to two in 2030.

sections.label: Total Fertility Rate fall
sections.summary: The Total Fertility Rate fell to 1.2 from 1.24 a year ago, due in large part to a larger cohort of young Singaporeans entering peak childbearing ages of 25-39 who have not yet started having children.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Our Total Fertility Rate (TFR) fell to 1.2, from 1.24 a year ago, due in large part to a larger cohort of young Singaporeans who are now entering the peak childbearing ages of 25-39 years, but who have not yet started having children.

sections.label: Parental leave and family measures
sections.summary: Together with parental leave enhancements taking effect this year, these measures will help young Singaporean couples get a place of their own earlier and enjoy better support, benefiting about 25,000 families annually.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Together with the parental leave enhancements that will take effect this year, these measures will help young Singaporean couples get a place of their own earlier, have better peace of mind in caring for their babies and enjoy better workplace and community support in their parenthood journeys.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We expect the enhancements to benefit about 25,000 families annually.

sections.label: PPS first-timer BTO success
sections.summary: First-timer PPS applicants were twice as likely to succeed in BTO and SBF flat applications as first-timer non-PPS applicants.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Last year, first-timer PPS applicants were twice as likely to be successful in their BTO and SBF flat applications as compared to first-timer non-PPS applicants.

sections.label: PPHS benefits for parents
sections.summary: PPHS has benefited about 2,000 families, and 400 babies have been born to families living in PPHS flats.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As pointed out by Mr Darryl David and Ms Tin, PPHS has, indeed, been a helpful scheme for parents.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: So far, it has benefited about 2,000 families, and 400 babies have been born to families living in PPHS flats.

sections.label: Resale flat grants up to $110,000
sections.summary: Couples buying resale flats can henceforth enjoy up to $110,000 in grants.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Couples buying resale flats can, henceforth, enjoy up to $110,000 in grants.

sections.label: Second week of paternity leave
sections.summary: From this year, the law provides for a second week of paternity leave.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: From this year, the law provides for a second week of paternity leave.

sections.label: Public sector parental and infant care leave
sections.summary: Public sector officers and spouses get six months parental leave per couple, plus four weeks unpaid infant care leave per parent from July.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Under this pilot, public sector officers and their spouses will be guaranteed six months of parental leave per couple.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: From July this year, the Public Service will provide an additional four weeks of unpaid infant care leave per parent, to be taken within the child's first year.

sections.label: MOM Work-Life Grant for FWAs
sections.summary: The Government will continue supporting them through resources including MOM's Work-Life Grant, which provides up to $160,000 for FWAs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The Government will continue to support them through various resources, including MOM's Work-Life Grant, which provides up to $160,000 to help companies implement FWAs.

sections.label: Community bonding and family-friendly plans
sections.summary: A virtual kampong became a tight community, and PA will share plans to celebrate families and make public transport more family-friendly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: What was originally a "virtual kampong" to exchange child-minding tips is now a fairly tight community that comes together regularly to celebrate the Mid-autumn Festival or dress up for Halloween parties.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The People's Association (PA) has some ideas on how we can bring communities together to celebrate families in a bigger way.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: PA will share more in a few weeks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State, Prime Minister's Office (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: We also have plans to make our public transportation more family-friendly.

sections.label: Public sector parental leave pilot
sections.summary: The Government will pilot six months of guaranteed parental leave per couple for public sector officers and spouses, benefiting up to 25,000 families yearly.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Government will launch a pilot where public sector officers and their spouses will be guaranteed six months of parental leave per couple, so that they will have more time to adjust to the new addition in the family.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The package of enhancements to be implemented this year will benefit up to 25,000 families annually when fully rolled out.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The Government will set aside an additional $140 million per year to implement these measures.

sections.label: Marriage and parenthood enhancement costs
sections.summary: Enhancements after this year's COS will benefit an estimated 25,000 families annually and cost an additional $140 million a year.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The package of enhancements to be implemented after this year's COS will benefit an estimated 25,000 families annually, when fully rolled out, and cost the Government an additional $140 million a year.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This comes on top of the $2.5 billion each year that is set aside to support marriage and parenthood.

sections.label: MAS 1MDB enforcement actions
sections.summary: MAS shut down BSI and Falcon Singapore branches, fined other banks, and set up anti-money laundering and enforcement departments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: BSI, one of Switzerland's oldest private banks, had its Singapore branch shut down by MAS in May 2016, because it was the custodian bank for $2.3 billion of investments from 1MDB.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Singapore branch of Falcon Private Bank, another private Swiss bank, was also shut down by MAS in October 2016 after being linked to US$3.8 billion of 1MDB fund flows.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Standard Chartered Bank was fined, while both UBS and DBS were penalised by MAS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In June 2016, MAS announced that it would combat money laundering by strengthening enforcement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: This included the setting up of a dedicated anti-money laundering department, a dedicated supervisory team to monitor risks and carry out on-site supervision of financial institutions, and a new enforcement department to work jointly with CAD.

sections.label: Singapore's first 1MDB enforcement actions
sections.summary: Singapore was first to take enforcement actions, shutting down BSI and Falcon Bank, penalising institutions, and fining or imprisoning individuals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In the case of the 1MDB-related transactions, we were the first jurisdiction in the world to take enforcement actions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We shut down two banks mentioned by Ms Sylvia Lim – BSI and Falcon Bank – and imposed financial penalties on several other financial institutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Our courts have fined and, in some cases, imprisoned individuals who were complicit.

sections.label: ABS Responsible Financing Guidelines
sections.summary: Since 2015, ABS member banks are expected to factor sustainability issues into their lending and investment policies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Since the launch of ABS' Responsible Financing Guidelines in 2015, ABS member banks are expected to factor into their lending and investment policies sustainability issues, such as greenhouse gas emissions, deforestation, resource efficiency, labour standards and corporate integrity.

sections.label: Comply-or-explain regime flexibility
sections.summary: The comply-or-explain regime allows listed companies flexibility to use alternative governance approaches if deviations from the Corporate Governance Code come with meaningful explanations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The comply-or-explain regime recognises the need for flexibility and allows listed companies to adopt alternative ways to achieving good governance, as long as deviations from the Corporate Governance Code are accompanied by meaningful explanations.

sections.label: Council review of comply-or-explain
sections.summary: The Council will review and consult widely on making the comply-or-explain regime more effective, considering business, investor and international factors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: The Council will review how the comply-or-explain regime can be made more effective.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: It will consult widely to ensure that business considerations, investor feedback, as well as international developments, are taken into account.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Ultimately, the review seeks to ensure that the Corporate Governance Code continues to support sustained corporate performance, business growth and innovation and maintain investor confidence in our capital markets.

sections.label: MAS unclaimed funds and Public Service scenarios
sections.summary: MAS is studying a framework for unclaimed funds and ways to help individuals locate inactive accounts, while Public Service scenarios cover national issues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: MAS has been studying the need for a formalised framework to deal with such unclaimed funds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) and Second Minister for Defence (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: In the meantime, MAS is studying ways to help individuals locate their inactive accounts, with a view to reducing such unclaimed funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: Yes, Mdm Chairperson, the Public Service still does that.

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: It is now under the PMO Strategy Group and these scenarios cover the entire range of issues which the Public Service and, indeed, Singapore need to deal with − economic, security, social, family and population issues as well.

sections.label: Resources for public servants
sections.summary: Resources will continue to be provided as needed and available to the Public Service to support officers in their work.

sentences.speaker: The Chairman
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Teo, do you want to respond to that − how the cut will affect individual public servants?

sentences.speaker: Mr Teo Chee Hean
sentences.text: We will continue to provide resources as needed and as available to the Public Service to support our officers in the work that they do.

sections.label: New citizens and secret votes
sections.summary: The member asks whether a write-up on secret voting should be inserted in the new citizen guidebook, citing 20,000 new citizens a year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Would the Senior Minister of State further not recognise that with 20,000 new citizens a year, this is equivalent to one SMC, one GRC for parliamentary term, the consequences to our democracy will be grave if a significant minority, even the majority of them, do not understand that their votes are secret?

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: Given that, and my clarification, the third point is: would the Senior Minister of State agree to insert a short write-up in the new citizen guidebook explaining how votes are kept secret during the electoral process and, if not, why not?

sections.label: FATF report on money laundering
sections.summary: The member asks whether the FATF report said Singapore was not strong on cross-border bigger cases, before 1MDB findings and bank closures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: I have a clarification for Minister Ong Ye Kung on my cut on money laundering.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: He mentioned in his response that the Financial Action Task Force (FATF) had done an evaluation last year and generally gave a good report on our measures.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: But is it also not true that in that report, they actually said that while we were probably good at tackling smaller scale financial crime, we were not strong on cross-border, the bigger cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: There was an observation that we should try to target the more complex cases and that is expected of us as a sophisticated financial centre.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
sentences.text: If I remember correctly, when FATF made those observations, that was before we disclosed our findings on 1MDB money laundering and closed down BSI and Falcon Bank.
